clue.text: Child that is pursuing a pirate

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: Captain William Kidd was a notorious pirate
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A youngster tags along behind a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiddie is an informal word for a small youngster.

clue.text: Watch out to detain seceding faction

parts.note: to keep someone is to hold or detain them
a cave is a political breakaway group, after the Cave of Adullam in the Bible

explanation.surface: A warning to look sharp and hold back a group of rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEP CAVE is old British schoolboy slang for keeping a lookout (Latin cave, beware).
explanation.definitionFit: Keep cave is schoolboy slang for standing lookout, ready to warn others.

clue.text: Delegates — found 29 turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to found a business is to set it up
the answer to 29 across is a newspaper boss, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: Delegates are discovered when the boss comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SET UP + ED to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it on to an agent, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Drunkard mixed a beer in it

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of the following words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy has stirred a beer into something.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a noun for a habitual heavy drinker, a sot.

clue.text: In fall again, I held back fruit tree

indicators.note: the letter I goes in the reversed word for falling again
held back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: to relapse is to fall back into a former state

explanation.surface: Someone recalls holding back during a repeat tumble from a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns RELAPSE into ESPALER, and 'In' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or frame.

clue.text: Get a move on and tread the grapes?

definitions.meaning: slang for putting your foot on the accelerator
literally, stamping on grape juice when making wine

explanation.definitionFit: Juice is slang for fuel, so stepping on it means accelerating; winemakers literally stamp on grapes.

clue.text: Humiliate a menial

parts.note: base can mean lowly or menial

explanation.surface: Humiliating a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to degrade or humble them.

clue.text: Not appreciating where to find hot dogs?

definitions.meaning: ... as an old adjective means ungrateful
firedogs, the iron supports for logs, sit in a fireplace grate, and get hot

explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is ungrateful; split, the word gives the location of firedogs in a hearth.

clue.text: Staggered, having wound

definitions.meaning: ... also means wound a line on to a reel

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are past tenses: lurching unsteadily, and winding line on a spool.

clue.text: How women proceed when they get into habits

definitions.text: How women proceed when they get into habits

parts.words: How women proceed when they get into habits
parts.note: habits here are riding habits, worn by women who traditionally sat with both legs on one side of the horse, not nuns' robes

explanation.definitionFit: Women in riding habits traditionally sat with both legs on one side of the horse.

clue.text: Presidential oath that was removed from the record

definitions.text: Presidential oath that was removed from the record

parts.words: Presidential oath that was removed from the record
parts.note: Nixon's Watergate transcripts famously replaced his swearing with the words 'deleted'

explanation.definitionFit: The Watergate transcripts printed 'expletive deleted' in place of Nixon's swear words.

clue.text: Possibly obtuse Germanic settler

definitions.meaning: an obtuse one is between 90 and 180 degrees
the ... were a Germanic people who settled in England

explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse is one kind of geometric corner measure, and the Angles gave England its name.

clue.text: Lakeside shelter for exclusive group

parts.note: a cot or cote is a small shelter for animals
Lake Erie, set at the side of the shelter

explanation.surface: A hut by the water serves as a club's private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lakeside' tells you to put the lake (ERIE, one of the North American Great Lakes) beside the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small select circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Note on musical entertainment or work in theatre

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means added after the other piece

parts.note: an opera is a sung stage work
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note placed on a show or a stage job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work in theatre' is the operating theatre, where a surgeon operates.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons perform procedures in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Light underwear article

parts.note: in Britain a vest is an undershirt
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A flimsy undergarment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is not about weight: a vesta is an old word for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is a short wax match, used to strike a flame.

clue.text: Pushes in from side turn, awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly means the letters of the preceding words are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver barges in after an awkward turn from a side road.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to force your way in where you are not wanted.

clue.text: Taken out of net, without line being disentangled

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around L

parts.note: unsnared means freed from a snare or net

explanation.surface: A fish freed from the net, with the line untangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so UNSNARED goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsnarled means freed of tangles or knots.

clue.text: Top rigging needed in a sou'wester, say

parts.note: the head is the top of something
gear is equipment or tackle, like a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: A sailor needs a waterproof hat and rigging at the masthead.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat; it is not the wind here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is an example of a waterproof hat with a broad back brim.

clue.text: Come first against good player 1 (so-called)

indicators.note: so-called says the words are spoken, giving something that sounds like the entry

parts.note: against is anti, and a good player ranked in the draw is a seed

explanation.surface: Being first to face the number one seed.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a seed is a top-ranked player placed in the draw so the best players meet late.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to go before in time or order.

clue.text: Goddess depicted in Meissen bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the porcelain name are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A deity is portrayed as a porcelain bust from the German factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German porcelain maker; 'bust' looks like a sculpture but means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the Greek deity of retribution.

clue.text: Plant forming end of herbaceous border

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener plants something at the end of a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grasslike marsh plant.

clue.text: Extremely foolish fuss about honour

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss surrounds the honour

parts.note: dust, as in kick up a dust, means a commotion
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: The most stupid fuss about an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbest is the superlative of dumb, stupid, so most stupid.

clue.text: Ideal place to give up drug is in first-class university

indicators.note: in a down entry, give up means the whole lot is read upwards
in puts the drug inside the first-class university letters

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: The perfect spot for quitting drugs is a top university.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic shorthand for first-class (from Lloyd's ship register), written here as AI; 'give up' turns the whole assembly, not just the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society, from Thomas More's book.

clue.text: Casual worker has a lot of time for painting

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A temp has plenty of time to paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting method using pigment bound in egg yolk.

clue.text: Admit, being upset, forsaken by sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: lorn is an old word for forsaken or forlorn
the heart of the word sweet is the letter E

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, distressed at being dumped by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' reverses LORN + E (LORNE) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to admit them as a member.

clue.text: Like a bust exposed?

parts.note: a sculpted bust has no arms

explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted bust shows head and shoulders only, so it lacks arms, like someone defenceless.

clue.text: Baffling question for one being put in the picture

definitions.text: one being put in the picture
definitions.meaning: someone who sits for a portrait

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzle, and also a person sitting for an artist.

clue.text: How a woman looks having taken the plunge?

definitions.text: How a woman looks having taken the plunge?

parts.words: How a woman looks having taken the plunge?
parts.note: the plunge is not a dive or marriage but a plunging neckline

explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut neckline is called plunging, baring the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: A bishop found 'the answer and granted remission

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to find the answer to a puzzle is to have solved it

explanation.surface: A bishop worked out the reply and forgave sins.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to grant forgiveness of sins, remission.

clue.text: Boss who shares opinions with leaders

definitions.text: Boss who shares opinions with leaders

parts.words: Boss who shares opinions with leaders
parts.note: leaders are newspaper leading articles, written under the paper's chief

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's chief sets its views, expressed in leading articles.
